references.text: Moses mentions that the people number 600,000 foot soldiers, which explains his doubt about whether there is enough meat for all of them.
The Lord's question to Abraham about whether anything is too hard for the Lord, paralleling Moses' doubt about God's ability to feed the people.
Elisha's servant asks a similar question about how little food can satisfy many people, and God performs a miracle.
An officer expresses similar doubt about God's ability to provide food in abundance, even though the Lord has opened windows in heaven.
The psalmist refers to the people's doubt in the wilderness: 'Can God set a table in the wilderness?' and asks if He can give bread and meat.
The disciples express similar doubt about how they can feed a large crowd before Jesus performs the miracle of the loaves.
The disciples ask again how one can feed so many people in the desert, reflecting Moses' doubt.
Philip and Andrew express doubt about how they can provide enough food for the crowd, similar to Moses' reaction.
